clue.text: Caribbean restriction on copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a ban is a prohibition or restriction

explanation.surface: A Caribbean government imposes an embargo on copper exports.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the restriction after the copper, so CU comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Cuba, the largest island nation in the region, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Prolonged episode of rigidity? Case aptly treated!

indicators.note: treated suggests the words Case aptly are processed and worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a patient's long rigid spell and congratulates themself on handling it well.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'Case aptly treated!' reads as a medical boast, but 'treated' is the anagram signal on CASE APTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is a trance-like state in which the body and limbs hold fixed for long periods.

clue.text: One of the rabble put a shilling on final

parts.note: a bob was slang for one shilling in old British money
the tail is the end or final part of something

explanation.surface: A ruffian bets a shilling on the last race of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' for a shilling (an old British coin, twelve pence) is a standard crossword convention; 'put ... on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'ragtag and bobtail' means the common riffraff, so a member of that crowd is one of the mob.

clue.text: Those against one's development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters of one's grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Opponents argue against someone's personal growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'one's' is ignored: its letters O, N, E, S are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary vote, the negative votes or the people casting them are counted against the motion.

clue.text: Cinemas do turn out such clowns

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters of Cinemas do are turned into something else

explanation.surface: Picture houses produce funny men as their stock in trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' reads as 'produce', but it is the anagram signal on CINEMAS DO; 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic entertainers who make audiences laugh are jokers or clowns.

clue.text: What, in gourmet recipe, is appetizing?

indicators.note: a recipe is a set of instructions for mixing ingredients, so the letters of What in gourmet are mixed

explanation.surface: A diner asks what it is in a fine-dining recipe that makes it so tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' is an unusual anagram signal: a recipe mixes ingredients, here the thirteen letters of WHAT IN GOURMET.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that makes the saliva flow because it looks or smells delicious is tempting and appetizing.

clue.text: Extinct Bird Act II?

indicators.note: II is the Roman numeral two, so the word for act appears twice

parts.note: to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: The second act of a play called Extinct Bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act II' looks like a stage direction, but the Roman numeral II means take the word for 'act' twice.
explanation.definitionFit: This flightless creature from Mauritius died out in the seventeenth century and is the classic example of extinction.

clue.text: Mechanic can't begin to be biased

indicators.note: can't begin tells us the word for biased loses its opening letter

parts.note: a partisan view is one-sided or biased

explanation.surface: A workman says he can't start because he is prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker or craftsman, an old sense of the word mechanic.

clue.text: Southern border of grass

parts.note: an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: A strip of lawn edges the southern side of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: This grasslike plant of marshes and wet ground is loosely called a grass.

clue.text: Plain gold representation, still, on stage

parts.note: a table, as in tableland, is a flat elevated stretch of land
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A plain golden image is displayed motionless on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for 'gold', but it is the noun for flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a living picture: actors posed silent and motionless to depict a scene.

clue.text: A French training programme of note proves wayward

parts.note: un is French for a
discipline is a system of training
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A French course for musicians turns out to be badly behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'proves' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is wayward follows no rules and lacks self-control, so is unruly.

clue.text: At university, made appointment to be fully briefed

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford
to date someone is to make an appointment to go out with them

explanation.surface: A student arranges a meeting so as to get properly informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brought up to date has been given all the latest information.

clue.text: Behold commercial cargo

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: Look at the cargo featured in an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is the goods carried by a vehicle or ship, its freight.

clue.text: Part of Florida hot, in a state

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of Florida is hot, and someone is in a state about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in a state' as the definition, but 'in' is a link word: the answer is a state, not 'in a state'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty US states, in the mountainous north-west.

clue.text: I'll speak of Avalon or Skye

indicators.note: speak of signals that the word I'll is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the contraction for I will

explanation.surface: Someone promises to talk about two romantic islands of legend and the Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: Avalon is the legendary island of the Arthurian tales; Skye is a Scottish Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are islands, each an example of a small island.

clue.text: Fight mainly clean

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word for clean, dropping its last letter

parts.note: to scrape a surface is to clean it

explanation.surface: Boxers fight mostly by the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a brawl or scuffle.

clue.text: County flags

definitions.meaning: The standard abbreviation for Wiltshire, an English county in the south-west
flags here is a verb, meaning droops or loses energy

explanation.definitionFit: The county is Wiltshire, shortened; and one who flags droops like a thirsty plant.

clue.text: Fresh pilot notices a nick

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of pilot notices a are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A new pilot spots a scratch on the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for a police station (and for prison), not a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, being taken down the nick means going to the local police headquarters.

clue.text: Heels were repaired in another place

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters of Heels were are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cobbler fixed the heels at a different shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means somewhere other than here, at a different location.

clue.text: In the wind, they blow over reeds

definitions.text: In the wind, they blow over reeds

parts.words: In the wind, they blow over reeds
parts.note: reads like gusts sweeping across a marsh, but the wind is the orchestra's woodwind section and the reeds are the mouthpieces players blow across

explanation.surface: Gales sweep across the rushes of a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a breezy marsh; really the wind section of an orchestra holds players who blow single-reed instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a single-reed woodwind instrument sit in the orchestra's wind section.

clue.text: Vehicle works with Masefield's lines

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a machine that goes is one that works or functions

explanation.surface: A car is running, accompanied by lines from the poet Masefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces. John Masefield's best-known poem begins 'Quinquireme of Nineveh from distant Ophir'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous poem by John Masefield, Poet Laureate, about ships and their freight.

clue.text: Member of the Goose foot family nips back to a club house

definitions.text: Member of the Goose foot family

indicators.note: back tells us the word nips is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
H is a common abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A goose nips back towards the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIPS into SPIN; 'to' is a link. The goosefoot family is the botanical family that includes beet and spinach.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy green vegetable belongs to the goosefoot group of plants, now within the amaranth family.

clue.text: Stopper for port

definitions.meaning: a bung made from bark, used to seal a bottle
a harbour city on the south coast of Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: A bottle bung is made from this bark, and the same name belongs to a harbour city in southern Ireland.

clue.text: Constable, artist and oil-producer

parts.note: a cop is a police constable
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: John Constable the painter, another artist, and an oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' and 'artist' suggest the landscape painter, but Constable is a police officer here; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried coconut kernel is pressed to yield coconut oil.

clue.text: Flat, open country

definitions.meaning: a wide expanse of level land

explanation.definitionFit: The word means level or unadorned, and also a broad treeless lowland.

clue.text: Compete with women following examination

indicators.note: following places the women after the word for compete

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Women compete after an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a view is to inspect it, so it means an inspection or survey.

clue.text: Canon gives 100 lines

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
an ode is a poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A churchman composes a hundred lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a body of rules or law, as is a code.

clue.text: Archduke, we hear, is something of a patriot

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a part of the word patriot

explanation.surface: An archduke is supposedly a bit of a nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Archduke is a piano trio, a piece we hear. 'we hear' is part of the definition, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Archduke is a chamber piece for piano, violin and cello: a work for three players.

clue.text: eg She is in favour of sister carrying oxygen

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: carrying means the nun holds the oxygen inside her

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: She is a supporter of the sister who carries the oxygen tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' reads as a woman, but the definition is the word she itself; 'is' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a word standing in for a noun, the grammatical class it belongs to.

clue.text: Bishop in petrol station finds rubbish

indicators.note: in places the bishop inside the word for petrol station

parts.note: a garage sells petrol
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop in a filling station discovers litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is a mainly American word for household waste or trash.

clue.text: Headless rodent will hold back the water in Holland

definitions.note: the definition is a place in Holland, a city rather than a phrase

indicators.note: headless means the word for rodent loses its first letter

parts.note: a hamster is a rodent kept as a pet
a dam is a barrier that holds back water

explanation.surface: A rodent missing its head will block the canals of Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is a link. The definition is loose: the answer is a place in Holland, and the surface's Dutch dykes and dams make it apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital of the Netherlands, a city lying in the province of North Holland.

clue.text: Pigment used in Kirk intilloch rectory

indicators.note: used in says the answer is found inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A colour is used in the rectory at Kirkintilloch.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirkintilloch, printed here split in two, is a town near Glasgow; the answer runs across its end into 'rectory'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment made from iron oxide clay.
